data.title: Chat: message permalinks — expose message ids in the UI, anchor-link references

data.body: Origin: board DM msg 222 (human:forrest, 2026-08-30 21:15) — created on behalf of the board. Requirement: (1) every rendered message in the chat UI displays its message number alongside the message; (2) when a message body references another message by number/name (e.g. 'msg 156', '[218]'), the reference renders as an anchor link that navigates to and highlights the target message; (3) deep links survive refresh — build on the AS-9 query-string URL state so a message anchor is addressable in the URL. Cross-conversation references should at minimum work within the current conversation; linking across conversations is a planning-stage decision. Left in backlog — planning runs in a later tick.

Board directive (DM msg 230, human:forrest): implementation kickoff is now implicit for internal-tools work — no per-task board green-light needed. Marcus implements. Normal lifecycle still applies (plan -> implement -> QA review); what's removed is the per-task board wait, not the gates. AS-26 goes first; AS-27 lands on top of it.

Plan migrated to master from branch commit 1807a53 per the two-plane rule (2026-08-31 git methodology revision — board state lives on master, task branches carry code only). While migrating, folded in the board DM msg 241 scope per my msg 245 commitment: (a) repo *.md references in message bodies become links opening an in-app viewer, backed by a gated GET /api/file endpoint with a strict path allowlist (charset+segment checks, realpath prefix confinement, byte-identical 404 parity for all probe failures); (b) inline markdown styling (bold/italic/code/http-links) via a pure tokenizer, structure-first compose with the existing AS-ref/msg-ref passes, textContent-only — no innerHTML. Complexity raised medium -> high in the plan header. Branch feat/AS-26-message-permalinks recreated clean from master; worktree at .worktrees/AS-26 for Marcus.
Board greenlight to proceed (DM msg 280, human:forrest: "lets get these going"); acked as msg 281. Moving to in_progress — Marcus implements in .worktrees/AS-26 on feat/AS-26-message-permalinks.

Implemented: 7 commits on feat/AS-26-message-permalinks (c5e91da..fc78244), all six plan sections. 190/190 tests green (baseline 163, +27 new) — verified independently by the orchestrator in .worktrees/AS-26. Diff vs master is code-only (13 files, +1238/-56). Deviations: (1) store resolver named resolveMessage, not getMessage(id,me) — getMessage is already exported with an ungated contract and ~15 callers; (2) first msg-ref token includes the keyword ('msg 156' is the link text), list continuations are number-only; (3) file-ref match allows a trailing sentence period but never word chars (README.mdx never matches); (4) dead m with unresolvable t: both stripped; (5) file viewer gets section-6 styling only, no ref pass (message.refs does not exist for file content); (6) inline styling does not span newlines. CLI parity for /api/message/<id> deliberately out of scope per plan section 4. QA: hardest look at readRepoMarkdown() traversal gate ordering in server.js, and the browser-level behaviors unit tests cannot reach (scroll+highlight one-shot, repeat-click animation re-fire, popstate with ?c&t&m) — needs a manual pass against a server started from the worktree on a NON-8347 port; the live container must not be touched. Ready for QA.

QA REVIEW (qa-priya, cold read): VERDICT: FAIL — implementation-level rework needed. One acceptance criterion fails in the deployed container; everything else passes.

WHAT I REVIEWED/RAN: plan file + all 5 task comments; full diff master...feat/AS-26-message-permalinks (13 files, +1238/-56) read file-by-file in .worktrees/AS-26; full suite in a FRESHLY BUILT container (docker compose run --rm --build test): 190/190 pass — Marcus's claim independently confirmed. Then a scratch server from that exact image (docker run, port 18347, production-shaped mounts: .lattice:ro + personnel:ro at /repo, scratch DB; live 8347 container untouched and verified healthy after) for a live HTTP battery.

BLOCKING FINDING (criterion 5, plan §5): /api/file cannot serve the plan's named use cases in the only supported deployment. compose.yaml mounts ONLY .lattice/ and personnel/ under /repo (unchanged in this diff; image bakes CHAT_REPO_ROOT=/repo), so in the deployed container: README.md, PHILOSOPHY.md, CLAUDE.md, apps/chat/README.md → 404 'No such file.' (all live-verified on the scratch server), while .lattice/plans/task_01M1AP95DKSCGRMBPKSH0A5J2V.md and personnel/qa-priya-raman.md → 200. The plan's §5 names 'apps/chat/README.md' as the dominant idiom and its acceptance criterion requires the click to open the rendered file; a user clicking those refs in production gets 'That file isn't available.' This is the AS-17 failure class again, one layer up: 190 unit tests green (they pass a temp repoRoot) while the feature's headline path is dead at runtime. Not caught by any test because the suite is mountless by design. Rework: make the deployed container see the repo markdown the tokenizer links (e.g. mount the repo root :ro — the path gate already blocks non-.md, dot-leading segments incl. .worktrees/, and symlink escapes, so root-mount is compatible with the gate's design — or an equivalent Marcus/Owen prefer); update apps/chat/README.md 'Repo file links' section to state the served scope truthfully; add whatever deployment-shaped assertion is feasible. compose.yaml is code and belongs on this task branch.

WHAT PASSES (criteria 1-4, 6-10):
- STATIC_FILES/AS-17 check: /msg-refs.js and /markdown.js both in STATIC_FILES AND live-fetched 200 with text/javascript charset=utf-8 from the container; served app.js imports both; served index.html carries all 5 file-modal ids; api.test.js pins all of this (incl. a doesNotMatch on .innerHTML in served app.js). Exactly the standing rule.
- /api/message/<id> live: top-level → exact navigation shape (no body/author); reply carries threadRootId; missing me → 400; non-member probe of a #board msg vs id 99999 → byte-identical 404 {"error":"No such message."} (status+body compared as strings); member still resolves. store.test.js additionally covers foreign-DM parity and unknown-identity.
- /api/file gate: live probe battery (traversal, absolute, dot-leading, '.' segment, '//', case-sensitive .MD, .lattice bare, nonexistent) → all 404 byte-identical; unit tests also cover a REAL symlink escape (realpath prefix), a directory named dir.md, 600-char path, double-encoding, and the 512KB cap as a distinct 400. Gate ordering in readRepoMarkdown is correct: syntax → segments → realpath+isFile (one collapsed catch) → size; only size diverges, post-gate. Sound.
- XSS: zero innerHTML anywhere in public/ (verified in worktree grep AND in the served bundle); all assembly via el()/textContent/createTextNode; md-link hrefs anchored ^https?:// by the tokenizer (javascript:/data:/vbscript: unit-tested literal); msgref hrefs built from validated positive safe ints; permalink hrefs via the AS-9 serializer; viewer title/content textContent-only. No hole found.
- Client logic (code-verified): bodyNode is structure-first per §6 with AS→msg→file per-leaf order; applyAnchor shared one-shot with reflow-forced animation re-fire (edge 6); openThread/selectConversation/closeThread null anchorMsg ONLY on url:'push' so goToMessage's url:'none' sequencing preserves pre-set anchors (edge 10 intact); restoreFromUrl t+m compose with dead-param stripping; url-state.js comment + app README grammar updated.
- Tokenizers: unit coverage hits plan edges 7-8 and 14-16, round-trip asserted throughout; 'msgs 5/0' stops at invalid id; unsafe ints literal.
- Marcus's 6 declared deviations: all accepted. (1) resolveMessage naming — right call, getMessage is ungated with many callers; (2) keyword-in-first-token — satisfies exact-source-slice; (3) trailing sentence period on file refs — tested; (4) dead m with dead t both stripped — consistent with URL-as-projection; (5) viewer gets inline pass only — that IS what plan §5 says; (6) no cross-newline inline styling — sensible. CLI parity for the resolver out of scope per plan §4 — no objection for v1.
- Process: diff touches only apps/chat/**; no top-level md; all 7 branch commits authored developer-marcus-webb; board state on master. Two-plane rule holds.

NOT EXECUTABLE IN MY RIG (flagged by Marcus, code-verified only): browser-gesture visuals — scroll+highlight one-shot, repeat-click animation re-fire, popstate walk with ?c&t&m. Logic all checks out against the AS-9 substrate; recommend a 2-minute human/UI spot-check ride along with the rework verification.

NON-BLOCKING (backlog-worthy, not v1 blockers — filed here so they are recorded, not litigated): (a) msg-refs.js has tokenizeMsgRefs's JSDoc stranded above FILE_RE — cosmetic misplacement, fix in rework if touching the file; (b) plan-sanctioned whitespace continuation means 'msg 5 76 trombones' linkifies 76 — consider requiring an explicit separator in v2; (c) ref passes inside [text](url) inner can nest <a> in <a> (plan-sanctioned; inner preventDefault wins on plain click — safe but quirky); (d) scheme allowlist is case-sensitive so [x](HTTPS://…) stays literal — conservative, fine as-is.

NO INLINE FIXES COMMITTED: the review fails, so nothing was touched on the branch; worktree left clean at fc78244. Scratch container and DB removed after the battery; live asc-chat-server-1 verified untouched (healthy, 200 on 8347).

Rework cycle 2 starting (developer-marcus, in .worktrees/AS-26). Scope per Review Cycle 1 Findings: (1) the mount design call — root :ro vs an explicit narrow set — made deliberately, reasoning to follow in the commit + closing comment; (2) deployed-shape test coverage the mountless suite structurally lacks; (3) truthful served-scope statement in apps/chat/README.md; (4) stranded JSDoc in msg-refs.js. Verification will be a fresh-build suite run plus a live HTTP battery against a production-shaped scratch container (not port 8347), per the cycle-1 lesson that green units are not deployment evidence.

Rework cycle 2 INTERRUPTED mid-implementation (Fable 5 rate limit terminated the implementer). Recording exact state so the next agent does not re-derive or double-apply.

DONE: the mount design call was made and reasoned. Chosen: repo root read-only (`../..:/repo:ro`) replacing the `.lattice`+`personnel` pair in apps/chat/compose.yaml. Reasoning on record — per-file binds were rejected on mechanics (Docker file binds pin inodes; git checkout replaces top-level .md files, yielding stale content or ENOENT, a silent-wrongness class worse than the 404 being fixed) and a directory allowlist was rejected because top-level README/PHILOSOPHY/CLAUDE are files, not directories, so it cannot express them and regrows this bug on the next cited path. The gate (readRepoMarkdown, server.js) is the sole endpoint boundary and is strict: .md regular files only, every dot-leading segment rejected except a first '.lattice' (so .git/.claude/.worktrees are categorically unreachable), realpath containment defeats symlink escape, uniform 404s.

NOT DONE — this cycle is INCOMPLETE:
- test/deploy-shape.test.js does NOT exist. The comment now in compose.yaml says 'Pinned by test/deploy-shape.test.js — update both together.' That is a forward reference to a file that was never created. Either create it or correct the comment; do not leave it lying.
- apps/chat/README.md served-scope statement: untouched.
- Stranded tokenizeMsgRefs JSDoc in msg-refs.js: untouched.
- NO verification run. No suite run, no live HTTP fetch of repo-root markdown against a production-shaped container. Per the cycle-1 lesson, the fix is unproven until that battery runs.

STATE ON DISK: apps/chat/compose.yaml is modified but UNCOMMITTED in .worktrees/AS-26. Branch is unchanged at fc78244. Left uncommitted deliberately — it is a proposal, not an adopted change (see below). Do not treat it as reviewed work.

HELD FOR BOARD JUDGMENT: this widens what a network-reachable service can read from two directories to every non-dot-path .md in the repo, and the change was flagged by the safety classifier. The orchestrator declined to commit or push it autonomously. Risk is genuinely low (loopback + Tailscale-only binding, :ro at the kernel, repo content already on GitHub, gate blocks all dot paths) and the decision may well be right — but widening a service's read boundary is a board-visible call, not an implementer's default. Surfaced to human:forrest. Resume once he rules, or implement a narrower alternative if he prefers one.

Rework cycle 2 COMPLETE (developer-marcus, .worktrees/AS-26). Three commits on feat/AS-26-message-permalinks: c48d40c (mount + deploy-shape test), 439d12f (README served scope), 8d7a450 (stranded JSDoc). Branch fc78244 -> 8d7a450; worktree clean.

MOUNT: adopted as left on disk by the interrupted cycle — ../..:/repo:ro replacing the .lattice+personnel pair, per the board's ruling that repo-root read-only is approved. Not relitigated, not narrowed. The two alternatives are dead on measurement, and that is now in the commit message so nobody re-derives it: symlinks inside a mounted dir stay symlinks and resolve against the CONTAINER filesystem, so a link to an unmounted path dangles (ENOENT -> 404); hardlinks read fine at first but go silently stale because git checkout writes a new file and renames over it, leaving the directory entry a fresh inode while the link stays pinned to the old one (measured: README.md served v1 while the file was v2). Serving stale content is worse than the 404 being fixed.

DEPLOY-SHAPE TEST (test/deploy-shape.test.js, 4 tests). Parses compose.yaml and the Dockerfile as data — zero deps, a strict indentation-scoped YAML subset that THROWS on anything it does not recognise rather than shrugging, because a silently-empty parse would make every assertion vacuously pass. Extracts CHAT_REPO_ROOT from the Dockerfile ENV, builds a mount projection (longest container-prefix wins, as Docker resolves overlapping binds), and asserts, against a notional checkout root so the computation is lexical and identical on a host and inside the mountless container:
1. sanity/anti-vacuity — services parse as exactly [server, cli, test], server declares volumes.
2. THE ONE THAT MATTERS — /repo/{README.md, PHILOSOPHY.md, CLAUDE.md, apps/chat/README.md, .lattice, personnel} each project to their real repo-relative host location, mode ro. A narrowed mount makes the projection null and the assertion fails by name.
3. the mount at the baked root is the whole checkout and is :ro; /app/data is separately rw (chat's own state is not part of the read-only repo view).
4. cli keeps its narrow .lattice+personnel ro binds (it serves no /api/file, so narrow is correct there) and the test service still declares NO volumes — pinning the mountless property that caused the blind spot, so anyone who changes it must confront the comment.
It does NOT duplicate api.test.js's gate battery; scope is manifests only, stated in the header.

NARROWING PROVES IT FAILS: restored HEAD's narrow compose (git show HEAD:apps/chat/compose.yaml), ran the file, got 2 of 4 failing — "/repo/README.md must be mounted read-only from README.md" with actual null vs expected {host, mode:'ro'} — then restored the wide compose. That is the exact bug cycle 1 shipped, now caught by a test.

The manifests had to be COPY'd into the image (Dockerfile + .dockerignore un-ignore) or the assertions would only ever run on a developer's host and never in `docker compose run --rm --build test`, which is the standard runner — i.e. coverage that does not actually run, the cycle-1 failure mode restated. Confirmed running in-container: 4/4 from the built image.

TESTS: 190 before (suite minus deploy-shape, in the freshly built container — matches cycle 1's independently verified count), 194 after. `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 COMPOSE_DOCKER_CLI_BUILD=1 docker compose run --rm --build test` -> 194/194 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, 33.3s. Purely additive; my other three files are prose/comment-only.

LIVE HTTP (production-shaped scratch container, port 18348, NOT 8347): docker run of the branch-built image with the mount compose declares (<checkout>:/repo:ro), no host data mount so the scratch DB died with the container.
POSITIVE — all 200, content compared byte-for-byte against the host file:
  README.md            200  3078 B  sha 97c1622703f44bfa  matches host  "# The American Software Company"
  CLAUDE.md            200  32691 B sha 3fd79d25bf54af04  matches host  "# american-software-company"
  PHILOSOPHY.md        200  1745 B  sha a1a9232ca9a261fb  matches host  "# The American Software Company"
  apps/chat/README.md  200  26245 B sha 9f9126213c29cdfa  matches host  (4th, the plan's "dominant idiom")
Each echoed its own path back. These are the four paths that 404'd in cycle 1.
GATE — baseline nonexistent .md = 404 {"error":"No such file."}; every probe byte-identical to it:
  .git/config               404 identical
  .claude/settings.json     404 identical
  ../../../etc/passwd       404 identical
  apps/../../../etc/passwd  404 identical (extra: mid-path traversal)
  apps/chat/server.js       404 identical (non-.md inside the root)
  .git                      404 identical (extra: bare dot path)
  personnel                 404 identical (extra: directory, not a file)
CONTROL — pre-AS-26 scope intact: personnel/developer-marcus-webb.md 200 (2936 B), .lattice/plans/task_01M1AP95DKSCGRMBPKSH0A5J2V.md 200 (22132 B).
READ-ONLY — write from inside the container refused EROFS, and no stray file appeared in the checkout.
Scratch container stopped and removed (--rm); no scratch DB on the host. Live asc-chat-server-1 untouched throughout and verified after: 200 on 8347, 11 identities, still "Up (healthy)".

DEVIATIONS: (1) commits authored developer-marcus-webb, matching this branch's 7 existing commits and CLAUDE.md's own example, rather than the shorthand developer-marcus in my assignment — one branch, one author string. (2) The mount change and the test are ONE commit because compose's own comment says "update both together"; splitting them would leave a commit whose comment forward-references a nonexistent file, which is what the interruption left behind. (3) Dockerfile and .dockerignore now carry compose.yaml + Dockerfile into the image as test data — a real change beyond "add a test", justified above; nothing at runtime reads them. (4) I extended the probe battery past the four requested (7 gate probes, 4 positives, 2 controls, plus the EROFS check).

STILL OPEN, not mine to close: Priya's cycle-1 residual — browser-gesture visuals (scroll+highlight one-shot, repeat-click animation re-fire, popstate walk with ?c&t&m) remain code-verified only and want a short human UI pass. Status left in_progress; no merge, no push, per instructions.

QA REVIEW CYCLE 2 (qa-priya, rework-scoped). VERDICT: PASS. My cycle-1 blocking finding is closed — verified independently, not on report. One trivial prose fix applied inline and committed (f631077). Nothing else blocks. Cycle 2 of a 3-cycle limit; no further rework needed.

SCOPE: the three rework commits only (fc78244..8d7a450), per the 9/10 criteria I cleared in cycle 1. 6 files, +263/-24. I did not re-review the feature from scratch.

=== 1. IS THE FINDING CLOSED? YES — verified the way I found it. ===
Built the branch under a QA-only tag (asc-qa-as26-cycle2:local, --platform linux/amd64, so the live asc-chat-server image tag was never touched), ran it on port 18349 with the mount compose now declares — the MAIN checkout at /repo:ro, which is the true production shape since compose runs from apps/chat and ../.. is the main checkout. Scratch DB ephemeral (no data mount). All four paths that 404'd in cycle 1 now serve, content sha256'd against the host file:
  README.md            200  4105 B  sha 71fd2c3532039470  MATCH  echo=ok
  PHILOSOPHY.md        200  1745 B  sha a1a9232ca9a261fb  MATCH  echo=ok
  CLAUDE.md            200  36380 B sha b7ef1a6d2ce54f22  MATCH  echo=ok
  apps/chat/README.md  200  21709 B sha 5fa323a1ed452020  MATCH  echo=ok
Controls (pre-AS-26 scope intact): personnel/qa-priya-raman.md 200 MATCH; .lattice/plans/task_01M1AP95DKSCGRMBPKSH0A5J2V.md 200 MATCH. My byte counts differ from Marcus's because he mounted the worktree root and master has advanced since; both are consistent — each served exactly what was at the mounted root.
END-TO-END, the check that actually closes criterion 5: fetched /msg-refs.js from the running container (200, text/javascript, byte-identical to the branch file), imported the SERVED bytes, ran tokenizeFileRefs over a realistic body — it emitted exactly ['apps/chat/README.md','README.md','PHILOSOPHY.md','CLAUDE.md'] with verbatim round-trip — then fetched each emitted path from that same container: 4/4 200 with correct first lines. The tokenizer's own output now resolves. In cycle 1 that same loop produced four "That file isn't available."
READ-ONLY genuinely enforced: writes from inside the container refused EROFS at top level and nested; rm refused; `mount` shows `/repo type fakeowner (ro,nosuid,nodev,relatime,fakeowner)`. No stray file in the checkout afterwards.

=== 2. DOES THE WIDER MOUNT OPEN ANYTHING? Probed hard. No. ===
62-probe adversarial battery against the production-shaped container, each compared as status+body STRING against a nonexistent-file baseline (404 {"error":"No such file."}). 61/62 byte-identical 404. Categories: dot-dirs now inside the mount (.claude/agents/qa-priya.md, .claude/settings.json, .git/config, .git/HEAD.md, .worktrees/AS-26/apps/chat/README.md, .gitignore, .env.md, .ssh/id_rsa.md — the ones the wide mount newly puts on the filesystem, all 404); dot-rule case variants (.Lattice, .LATTICE); bare dot paths; traversal (../, mid-path apps/../../../etc/passwd.md, ./ segments, .lattice/../); encoding (%2e%2e%2f, double-encoded %252e, %2f-absolute, %00 NUL truncation both before and after .md, %0a/%0d/%09, + and %20, backslash, fullwidth U+FF0E, U+2215 division-slash homoglyph, %c0%ae overlong); absolute and /repo-prefixed; non-.md (server.js, chat.db); case-varied suffix (.MD, .Md); directories (personnel, apps, apps/chat); empty and missing param; 512/513/5000-char paths. Also: duplicate ?path params are first-wins (searchParams.get), so a trailing hostile param cannot override a benign one — and a leading hostile one just 404s.
SYMLINK BATTERY, run against a purpose-built scratch root (18350) so the real checkout was never written to. All five escape vectors 404 byte-identically: symlink to /etc/passwd, symlink to ../outside/secret.md, symlink DIRECTORY to /etc then etcdir/hostname.md, symlink dir to ../outside, nested sub/deep-escape.md. Dangling symlink 404. Realpath containment is airtight — nothing outside the mounted root is reachable by any means I found. Special files: directory named dir.md 404, file inside it 404, FIFO named fifo.md 404 (isFile() catches it). Size cap behaves as specced: exactly 512 KB serves 200, 600 KB returns the distinct 400 {"error":"File too large."} — post-gate, so not an oracle for anything the 200 wouldn't already reveal.
ONE REAL OBSERVATION, non-blocking: the dot-segment rule is a check on the REQUESTED string, so a non-dot-named symlink pointing into a dot directory launders it. Demonstrated: `latticelink -> .lattice` served `latticelink/plans/p.md` 200. Containment is unaffected (the target must still resolve inside the checkout) and `find` shows the checkout contains NO symlinks at all, so this is hypothetical today — and anyone who could plant such a symlink already has repo write access, i.e. could just write the content into a .md directly. It gains an attacker nothing. But the wide mount is what makes it matter, so I recorded it in the README (inline fix below) and filed it as backlog, not a blocker. Hardening, if ever wanted: re-run the segment check on the realpath-relative path after resolution.
WHAT THE MOUNT NEWLY EXPOSES, enumerated rather than assumed: 32 .md files outside .lattice/personnel — the 4 headline paths, agents.md, apps/chat/watch/README.md, 6 test fixtures, and 20 docs/{strategy,design}/*.md. Grepped the whole set for credential shapes (private-key headers, api_key/secret/password assignments, ghp_ tokens): zero hits. Also worth recording: the AS-5 chat exports in apps/chat/data/export/ are .jsonl, NOT .md, so they are outside the gate entirely — the AS-6 private-channel exclusion is untouched by this mount.

=== 3. DOES deploy-shape.test.js BITE? YES — and the parser is not vacuous. ===
Verified Marcus's narrowing claim myself, in an isolated scratch copy of apps/chat (never dirtying the worktree): restored fc78244's narrow compose, ran the file -> exactly 2 of 4 fail, with the precise message he quoted: "/repo/README.md must be mounted read-only from README.md" actual null vs expected { host: '/checkout/README.md', mode: 'ro' }, plus "server mounts something at the baked CHAT_REPO_ROOT (/repo)" actual undefined. Confirmed.
Then attacked the hand-rolled YAML subset with 14 malformed/restructured manifests looking for a SILENT PASS. Found none — every one was detected, either by a thrown parse error or a failing assertion: flow-style `volumes: [...]`, long-form type/source/target mount mapping, mount present but rw (:ro dropped), mount commented out, mount widened to ../../.. (the PARENT of the checkout — caught, which means the test also pins the mount from getting wider than the board approved), services: key renamed, empty file, 4-space reindent, volumes nested one level deeper, a 4th service added, a trailing comment on a service line, mount pointed at /repo2, Dockerfile baking /srv, and a comment line containing CHAT_REPO_ROOT=/oldroot placed before the ENV. That last one is worth naming: the bakedRepoRoot regex IS first-match and WOULD capture a comment, but assert.equal(root,'/repo') catches it — it fails loud, never silently. Anti-vacuity test (services deepEqual ['server','cli','test'] + server has volumes + name: asc-chat) does its job.
Confirmed the 4 tests actually execute in-container, not just on a host: all four ✔ lines appear in the `docker compose run --rm --build test` log.

=== 4. Dockerfile/.dockerignore COPY of the manifests — assessed, acceptable. ===
Measured rather than reasoned: `docker history` shows the layer is 4.73 kB (compose.yaml 3631 B + Dockerfile 1097 B) on a 231 MB image — 0.002%, not meaningful bloat. Contents carry NO secrets: env var names and passthroughs (CHAT_BIND, LATTICE_DASHBOARD_URL, CHAT_API, CHAT_ME), a loopback-only port map, and prose. Grepped server.js, lib/, bin/, public/, watch/ for any reference to compose.yaml or Dockerfile: zero — his "nothing at runtime reads them" is confirmed, only test/ does. Not HTTP-reachable: STATIC_FILES is a fixed allowlist keyed on url.pathname reading from join(APP_DIR,'public',file), with no path-joining from user input; probed /compose.yaml, /Dockerfile, /app/compose.yaml, /../compose.yaml, /public/../compose.yaml -> all 404 {"error":"Not found."}. And /repo/apps/chat/compose.yaml is inside the wide mount but not .md, so the gate rejects it (probed). Layer-cache cost is trivial (the COPY sits before only a mkdir+chown). It is consistent with the file's established pattern — this image already ships test/ and watch/ for the same "the suite runs the exact bits the repo ships" reason, documented the same way in both places. Deviation accepted.
One limitation to name, not a blocker: the in-container assertions read the COPY'd manifests, so `docker compose run --rm test` WITHOUT --build could assert a stale compose. --build is what the README and the ./chat wrapper document, and the host-side `node --test` run reads the live files. This is the same staleness property every COPY'd test in this image already has, not something this change introduced.

=== 5. FULL SUITE ON A FRESH BUILD — confirmed. ===
DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 COMPOSE_DOCKER_CLI_BUILD=1 docker compose run --rm --build test -> tests 194, pass 194, fail 0, cancelled 0, skipped 0, todo 0, duration 33.9s. Exactly his number. Freshly built, not a cached image.

=== 6. README truthfulness + JSDoc — both good. ===
Walked every claim in the new "What it can actually serve" paragraph against measurement: whole-repo :ro mount (true), served scope = every *.md regular file under 512 KB (true), read-only at the kernel (true, EROFS), deploy-shape pins it (true). The env table row and the personnel/.lattice plumbing edits are accurate — I confirmed the CLI reads nothing beyond .lattice/personnel (no repoRoot/readFileSync/api-file usage in bin/chat.js), so "which is all it reads" is correct.
msg-refs.js: verified the JSDoc move is PURE. Stripped all comment lines from both fc78244 and HEAD versions and diffed — IDENTICAL. Zero code change. The JSDoc is back on tokenizeMsgRefs.

=== INLINE FIX COMMITTED (f631077, authored qa-priya) ===
apps/chat/README.md prose only, no behavior: the paragraph claimed .git/, .claude/ and .worktrees/ are "categorically unreachable". That is true for every path a client can NAME (61/62 probes prove it), but not literally categorical given the symlink-laundering mechanism above. Reworded to "unreachable by any path a client can name" and added a two-sentence caveat naming the mechanism and stating that the checkout has no symlinks today.
